target_customer: Android users, mostly under 25, who text heavily
problem: Messaging forces users to leave what they are doing; floating chat heads let them reply in place.
business_model: Free SMS replacement app with a paid version at $3.99

founders.name: Wael Nafee
previous_startups: OCR mobile app sold to a Saudi mobile operator

exit.reason: Not stated; Crunchbase lists it as closed

competitors.name: Facebook Home chat heads
competitors.traction_then: Launched about a week after HoverChat per TechCrunch

competitors.name: Go SMS Pro, Handcent SMS, mySMS
competitors.what: Third party Android SMS replacement apps

technical_complexity.rationale: Overlay windows and SMS handling on Android were well understood in 2014, though background services and privacy permissions needed care.

defensibility.rationale: Floating chat heads were copied by Facebook and easy for any SMS app to add; no network effect beyond SMS.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook shipped chat heads in Messenger, and Android later added bubbles natively (Android 11 per 9to5Google, 2020).

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported over 200,000 Google Play downloads and about 8,000 new downloads a day in March 2014, showing interest, but no revenue figures.

branding.name_origin: Descriptive of floating avatars called hoverheads; the app was first named Ninja SMS per TechCrunch and Engadget.
branding.domain_note: hoverchat.com now redirects to a domain sale page (HugeDomains).
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch, Engadget, 9to5Google and several blogs in 2014 as the first Egyptian YC startup.

brand_strength.rationale: Early press and 200,000 downloads, but no lasting brand.

outcome_analysis: HoverChat was an Egyptian founded Android SMS replacement that gained over 200,000 downloads in its first year and entered YC in Winter 2014. Its floating avatar idea resembled Facebook chat heads, which launched the week before, and the app depended on SMS with no network of its own. It is listed as closed with no stated cause, so the incumbent copying factor is an inference from the product position rather than a company statement.
notes: Cause of closure is not public in sources found; failure factor is an inference. Funding amount undisclosed, only described as small. Shutdown date unknown. Team size 11 per YC page.
